title: Iran’s Moment of Opportunity
content: America and Israel's unilateral aggression against Iran lacked international legitimacy and predictably destabilized the entire region. But as justified as the Iranian leadership might feel in pursuing an obstinately maximalist strategy, it must be careful not to mistake short-term advantages for longer-term gains.

title: Is Russia’s Placement on the Security Council Legal?
content: When Russia replaced the Soviet Union as a permanent member of the United Nations Security Council in 1991, it did not even attempt to follow the process outlined in the UN Charter. Now that Russia's usurpation of the USSR’s seat has enabled it to wage a war of aggression, the dubious legal status of its position must be revisited.

title: To Support Nepal, Waive Remittance Fees
content: To help Nepal move from rescue and relief toward reconstruction, money-transfer companies and banks ought to waive fees on remittances sent to the country for at least two months. Doing so could provide additional relief totaling several times more than what a recent emergency appeal by the United Nations generated.

title: What a Canada–Europe Alliance Needs
content: With trade, finance, technology, and supply chains having all become instruments of coercion, Canada, Europe, and other likeminded democracies must come together to defend their interests. But strategic convergence between governments is not enough; if a new alliance is to endure, it needs deep roots in society.

title: Trump’s Great Oil Heist
content: Venezuela’s hopes for a democratic transition are fading as the US works to take control of its vast oil wealth. Billions in US and foreign investment could strengthen the chavista regime and give future American presidents powerful incentives to preserve the political status quo.

title: Global AI Oversight Now
content: AI is already concentrating enormous economic power and deepening existing inequalities, yet governments lack the institutions and expertise needed to govern it. They should establish an international AI body that can set standards and coordinate a collective response to threats no country can handle alone.

title: Climate Resilience Starts With Care
content: Climate shocks can disrupt services that millions of vulnerable people rely on, yet care is largely absent from adaptation plans and national funding estimates. Investing in climate-resilient care can prevent cascading health and economic crises while creating jobs and easing pressure on public budgets.

content: For Seychelles and other countries across the Western Indian Ocean region, marine conservation is a fundamental component of national development. But the ocean observes no national borders, which makes international cooperation and common financing instruments essential.

content: With the global economy having weathered major trade and energy shocks over the past two years, growth should improve in 2027, and inflation should fall. Although various political and policy-driven risks could change the outlook, they remain less likely than the relatively benign baseline scenario.

title: Closing Europe’s Dynamism Deficit
content: Europe has built an economic framework that protects yesterday’s champions at the expense of tomorrow’s potential winners. To remain competitive, sovereign, and secure in the 21st century, it will need a new model geared toward promoting domestic innovation and commercialization at scale.

title: America’s Looming Debt Reckoning
content: High debt levels become dangerous when rising interest rates push up borrowing costs and governments fail to respond. With little political appetite to rein in its federal deficit and ballooning debt, the United States risks finding itself with few options when the next war, recession, or financial crisis arrives.

title: The OECD Should Be Reclaimed, Not Abandoned
content: In recent years, the OECD has strayed from its core mission of coordinating economic policy among the US and its allies, instead building programs around gender budgeting and environmental justice. The Trump administration should use its leverage at the organization to return its focus to economics and national security.

title: Putin Is Testing NATO at Ukraine’s Borders
content: The Kremlin is determined to isolate Ukraine, which means not only breaking the will of the country’s backers, but also cutting it off physically by striking merchant ships, ports, and border crossings. These assaults cannot go unanswered, because they embolden Russian President Vladimir Putin to continue testing the West.

content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has challenged the world’s middle powers to build a better international order. content: For the first time, all the UK’s political parties on the right favor withdrawing from the European Convention on Human Rights. But the story of the Hillsborough Law shows how human-rights laws, not least the ECHR, help ordinary people hold the state accountable for its costliest failings.

title: Will AI Reverse the Renminbi’s Rise?

title: The Price of You
content: As more people shop online, firms are increasingly setting individualized prices based on personal data, including purchase history, location, demographics, behavior, and biometric data. AI threatens to turbocharge such surveillance pricing, further widening the gap between privacy expectations and reality.
